explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about the library's own definition `TauCeti.symmetricEntry`, the symmetric matrix `(1/2) • (single i j 1 + single j i 1)`, and Mathlib has no such object. The proof combines several general Mathlib lemmas (`Matrix.trace_single_mul`, `Matrix.trace_add`, `Matrix.trace_smul`, `Matrix.smul_mul`, `Matrix.add_mul`) with the symmetry of a Hermitian matrix (`IsHermitian.apply`). No single Mathlib declaration states the result, even as an instance of something more general. `Matrix.trace_single_mul` covers only one of the two terms, and the proof also needs the averaging step and the symmetry step. The mathematical content therefore lies in the library's definition, not in a Mathlib theorem.
